citations.quote: Let $X$ be a set. A finite multiset on $X$ is a function $m:X\to\mathbb N_0$ with finite support $\operatorname{supp}(m)=\{x\in X:m(x)>0\}$. The multiplicity $m(x)$ is the number of occurrences of $x$, and the size is $|m|=\sum_{x\in\operatorname{supp}(m)}m(x)$. Two finite multisets are equal exactly when their multiplicity functions agree at every element of $X$. We write $\{\!\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}\!\}$ for the multiset whose multiplicity at $x$ is the number of indices $i$ with $x_i=x$; $n=0$ denotes the empty multiset.

citations.quote: Let $G=(V,E,\ell)$ and $H=(W,F,m)$ be finite vertex-labeled simple undirected graphs with labels in the same set $\Sigma$. A label-preserving graph isomorphism from $G$ to $H$ is a bijection $\varphi:V\to W$ such that $\ell(v)=m(\varphi(v))$ for every $v\in V$, and for all distinct $u,v\in V$, $\{u,v\}\in E$ if and only if $\{\varphi(u),\varphi(v)\}\in F$. The graphs are isomorphic when such a bijection exists, and nonisomorphic otherwise.

Let $G=(V,E,\ell)$ and $H=(W,F,m)$ be finite vertex-labeled simple undirected graphs with labels in a common set $\Sigma$. Define color sets recursively by $C_0=\Sigma$ and $C_{t+1}=C_t\times\mathsf M_{\mathrm{fin}}(C_t)$ for each integer $t\ge0$. Set $c_0^G(v)=\ell(v)$ and $c_0^H(w)=m(w)$; for $t\ge0$, update

$$ c_{t+1}^G(v)=\left(c_t^G(v),\{\!\{c_t^G(u):u\in N_G(v)\}\!\}\right),\qquad c_{t+1}^H(w)=\left(c_t^H(w),\{\!\{c_t^H(z):z\in N_H(w)\}\!\}\right). $$

The graph color multiset at round $t$ is $C_t(G)=\{\!\{c_t^G(v):v\in V\}\!\}$, and likewise for $H$. One-dimensional Weisfeiler–Leman color refinement distinguishes $G$ and $H$ at round $t$ when $C_t(G)\ne C_t(H)$; it distinguishes the pair when this holds for some finite $t$. If no finite round distinguishes them, they are one-WL-indistinguishable. In the unlabeled case, take $\Sigma$ to be a singleton. The tuple update is the canonical collision-free color encoding.

Let $X$ be a set. A finite multiset on $X$ is a function $m:X\to\mathbb N_0$ with finite support $\operatorname{supp}(m)=\{x\in X:m(x)>0\}$. The multiplicity $m(x)$ is the number of occurrences of $x$, and the size is $|m|=\sum_{x\in\operatorname{supp}(m)}m(x)$. Two finite multisets are equal exactly when their multiplicity functions agree at every element of $X$. We write $\{\!\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}\!\}$ for the multiset whose multiplicity at $x$ is the number of indices $i$ with $x_i=x$; $n=0$ denotes the empty multiset.

derivations.claim: By induction on $t$, $c_t^G(v)=c_t^H(\varphi(v))$ for every $v\in V(G)$. At $t=0$ this is label preservation from [F1]. If it holds at $t$, bijectivity and adjacency preservation in [F1] give a bijection $N_G(v)\to N_H(\varphi(v))$, and corresponding neighbors have equal round-$t$ colors by the induction hypothesis. Thus the neighbor-color multisets agree; the center colors agree as well, so the ordered-pair update [F2] gives equality at round $t+1$.

The same vertex bijection therefore sends every occurrence of each round-$t$ color in $G$ to an occurrence of that color in $H$, and its inverse gives the reverse correspondence. Hence the two graph color multisets have equal multiplicities for each color by [F3]. Their round-$t$ histograms agree for every finite $t$, so no round distinguishes them.

derivations.claim: By induction on $t=0,\ldots,K$, equal round-$t$ WL colors of vertices from either graph imply equal GNN states after $t$ layers. At $t=0$, the shared initial embedding gives this implication. If it holds at $t$ and two vertices have equal round-$(t+1)$ colors, [F2] says their center colors and neighbor-color multisets agree. By the induction hypothesis, equal neighbor colors have equal GNN states; applying this correspondence occurrence by occurrence gives equal neighbor-state multisets. The shared aggregation and update functions in [F1] therefore give equal next-layer states. Thus a well-defined map from each round-$t$ color occurring in either graph to its common GNN state exists.

At round $K$, the assumed equal WL color multisets become equal multisets of GNN states when each color is sent to its common state from step 1.1; multiplicities are preserved by [F3]. The shared graph readout in [F4] receives equal multisets, so the two graph outputs are equal. The contrapositive gives the stated distinguishing implication.

Let $G=(V,E,\ell)$ and $H=(W,F,m)$ be finite vertex-labeled simple undirected graphs with labels in a common set $\Sigma$. Define color sets recursively by $C_0=\Sigma$ and $C_{t+1}=C_t\times\mathsf M_{\mathrm{fin}}(C_t)$ for each integer $t\ge0$. Set $c_0^G(v)=\ell(v)$ and $c_0^H(w)=m(w)$; for $t\ge0$, update

$$ c_{t+1}^G(v)=\left(c_t^G(v),\{\!\{c_t^G(u):u\in N_G(v)\}\!\}\right),\qquad c_{t+1}^H(w)=\left(c_t^H(w),\{\!\{c_t^H(z):z\in N_H(w)\}\!\}\right). $$

The graph color multiset at round $t$ is $C_t(G)=\{\!\{c_t^G(v):v\in V\}\!\}$, and likewise for $H$. One-dimensional Weisfeiler–Leman color refinement distinguishes $G$ and $H$ at round $t$ when $C_t(G)\ne C_t(H)$; it distinguishes the pair when this holds for some finite $t$. If no finite round distinguishes them, they are one-WL-indistinguishable. In the unlabeled case, take $\Sigma$ to be a singleton. The tuple update is the canonical collision-free color encoding.

Fix a finite vertex-labeled simple undirected graph $G=(V,E,\ell)$, a finite nonnegative depth $K$, feature sets $H_0,\ldots,H_K$, and an initial map $\eta:\Sigma\to H_0$. For each $k=1,\ldots,K$, choose a set $Z_k$, an aggregation function $A_k:\mathsf M_{\mathrm{fin}}(H_{k-1})\to Z_k$ on finite multisets, and an update function $U_k:H_{k-1}\times Z_k\to H_k$. Initialize $h_v^0=\eta(\ell(v))$ and recursively set

$$
a_v^k=A_k\!\left(\{\!\{h_u^{k-1}:u\in N_G(v)\}\!\}\right),\qquad h_v^k=U_k(h_v^{k-1},a_v^k).
$$

For a chosen output set $Y$, a graph readout is a function $R:\mathsf M_{\mathrm{fin}}(H_K)\to Y$; the graph output is $z_G=R(\{\!\{h_v^K:v\in V\}\!\})$. The same maps are used on every graph being compared. The model has no vertex-identity input and uses no graph-wide information before the readout. It distinguishes two graphs when their outputs differ.

Let $\mathcal X$ be a countable set and let $M\in\mathbb N_0$. There is a map $\phi:\mathcal X\to\mathbb N_{>0}\subset\mathbb Q$ such that the sum $S\mapsto\sum_{x\in S}\phi(x)$ is injective on finite multisets $S$ of total multiplicity at most $M$. For every irrational $\varepsilon\in\mathbb R\setminus\mathbb Q$, the map

$$
(c,S)\longmapsto(1+\varepsilon)\phi(c)+\sum_{x\in S}\phi(x)
$$

is injective on pairs with $c\in\mathcal X$ and $S$ a finite multiset of total multiplicity at most $M$. For $M=0$, the only allowed neighbor multiset is empty.

Fix a finite depth $K\in\mathbb N_0$, positive integer dimensions $d_0,\ldots,d_K$, an initial embedding $\eta:\Sigma\to\mathbb R^{d_0}$, scalars $\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_K\in\mathbb R$, and maps $M_k:\mathbb R^{d_{k-1}}\to\mathbb R^{d_k}$ for $1\le k\le K$. Each $M_k$ is a multilayer perceptron, meaning a finite composition of affine maps between finite-dimensional real vector spaces and coordinatewise applications of a fixed scalar activation. On a finite vertex-labeled simple undirected graph $G$, initialize $h_v^0=\eta(\ell(v))$ and update

$$
h_v^k=M_k\!\left((1+\varepsilon_k)h_v^{k-1}+\sum_{u\in N_G(v)}h_u^{k-1}\right)\qquad(1\le k\le K).
$$

For a chosen output set $Y$, the graph readout is a map $R:\mathsf M_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathbb R^{d_K})\to Y$ on the multiset of final vertex features. The neighbor sum counts each neighbor vertex once, so equal feature vectors at different neighbors contribute with their multiplicity. This definition imposes no injectivity condition on the perceptrons or the readout and makes no claim that a fixed finite architecture realizes an arbitrary injection.

derivations.claim: For each $k\le K$, we prove that there is an injective map $\psi_k$ from the WL colors occurring at round $k$ in either graph to their GNN states. For $k=0$, use the initial embedding and [A1]. If this holds at $k-1$, a round-$k$ WL color has the form $(c,S)$ by [F1]. The injective map $\psi_{k-1}$ sends different center colors to different center states and, occurrence by occurrence, different neighbor-color multisets to different neighbor-state multisets. By [A2], their aggregates and then their updated states remain different whenever $(c,S)$ differs. Equal WL colors give equal states because the layer maps are shared functions. Thus the resulting round-$k$ state map $\psi_k$ is well-defined and injective.

The WL histograms at round $K$ differ by hypothesis. Applying the injective map $\psi_K$ to each color occurrence preserves multiplicities and keeps these two multisets different. The final node-state multisets therefore differ, and [A3] makes their graph readouts different by [F5].

If the active feature set is countable and neighbor multisets have size at most $\Delta$, apply [F3] with $M=\Delta$ to obtain the stated center/multiset preactivation code for any irrational $\varepsilon$. If each graph has at most $N$ vertices, apply the multiset part of [F3] with $M=N$ to obtain an injective sum code for final node-state multisets. Formula [F4] identifies the first code with the GIN preactivation when the current features use $\phi$; the injectivity of any post-MLP or readout realizing the full theorem remains the separate hypothesis [A2]–[A3].

citations.quote: Fix a set of labels $\Sigma$. A finite vertex-labeled simple undirected graph is a triple $G=(V,E,\ell)$ in which $V$ is a finite set of vertices, $E$ is a set of two-element subsets of $V$, and $\ell:V\to\Sigma$ assigns a label to each vertex. Its neighborhood at $v\in V$ is $N_G(v)=\{u\in V:\{u,v\}\in E\}$. Thus edges have no orientation, loops, or multiplicity. Graphs compared in one labeled-graph statement use the same label set $\Sigma$.

Let $G=(V,E,\ell)$ and $H=(W,F,m)$ be finite vertex-labeled simple undirected graphs with labels in the same set $\Sigma$. A label-preserving graph isomorphism from $G$ to $H$ is a bijection $\varphi:V\to W$ such that $\ell(v)=m(\varphi(v))$ for every $v\in V$, and for all distinct $u,v\in V$, $\{u,v\}\in E$ if and only if $\{\varphi(u),\varphi(v)\}\in F$. The graphs are isomorphic when such a bijection exists, and nonisomorphic otherwise.

Let $G=(V,E,\ell)$ and $H=(W,F,m)$ be finite vertex-labeled simple undirected graphs with labels in a common set $\Sigma$. Define color sets recursively by $C_0=\Sigma$ and $C_{t+1}=C_t\times\mathsf M_{\mathrm{fin}}(C_t)$ for each integer $t\ge0$. Set $c_0^G(v)=\ell(v)$ and $c_0^H(w)=m(w)$; for $t\ge0$, update

$$ c_{t+1}^G(v)=\left(c_t^G(v),\{\!\{c_t^G(u):u\in N_G(v)\}\!\}\right),\qquad c_{t+1}^H(w)=\left(c_t^H(w),\{\!\{c_t^H(z):z\in N_H(w)\}\!\}\right). $$

The graph color multiset at round $t$ is $C_t(G)=\{\!\{c_t^G(v):v\in V\}\!\}$, and likewise for $H$. One-dimensional Weisfeiler–Leman color refinement distinguishes $G$ and $H$ at round $t$ when $C_t(G)\ne C_t(H)$; it distinguishes the pair when this holds for some finite $t$. If no finite round distinguishes them, they are one-WL-indistinguishable. In the unlabeled case, take $\Sigma$ to be a singleton. The tuple update is the canonical collision-free color encoding.

Let $X$ be a set. A finite multiset on $X$ is a function $m:X\to\mathbb N_0$ with finite support $\operatorname{supp}(m)=\{x\in X:m(x)>0\}$. The multiplicity $m(x)$ is the number of occurrences of $x$, and the size is $|m|=\sum_{x\in\operatorname{supp}(m)}m(x)$. Two finite multisets are equal exactly when their multiplicity functions agree at every element of $X$. We write $\{\!\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}\!\}$ for the multiset whose multiplicity at $x$ is the number of indices $i$ with $x_i=x$; $n=0$ denotes the empty multiset.

derivations.claim: In $G$, vertex $i$ has the two distinct neighbors $i-1$ and $i+1$ modulo $6$. In $H$, each vertex has the other two vertices of its own triangle as neighbors. Thus every vertex in each graph has degree $2$.

At round $0$, all vertices of both graphs have color $\star$. If every vertex in both graphs has a common color $c_t$ at round $t$, then each vertex has the neighbor-color multiset with exactly two copies of $c_t$. The update [F3] therefore assigns the same ordered-pair color to every vertex in both graphs at round $t+1$. By induction, each graph has six copies of the same color at every round, so their color multisets agree and 1-WL never distinguishes them.

Suppose an isomorphism $\varphi:G\to H$ existed. Choose one vertex from each of the two triangles of $H$ and take their preimages under the surjection $\varphi$. In $G$ a finite sequence of cyclically consecutive vertices joins those preimages. Applying $\varphi$ to that sequence gives an edge path in $H$ by [F2], but $H$ has no edge between its triangles and hence no such path. This contradiction proves nonisomorphism.

derivations.claim: The number $\sqrt2$ is irrational: if $\sqrt2=p/q$ for coprime positive integers $p,q$, then $p^2=2q^2$ makes $p$ even, say $p=2s$, and substitution gives $q^2=2s^2$, so $q$ is even as well, contradicting coprimality.

By [F2], $J_{\sqrt2}(r,\{\!\{b\}\!\})=(1+\sqrt2)\cdot1+2=3+\sqrt2$, while $J_{\sqrt2}(b,\{\!\{r\}\!\})=(1+\sqrt2)\cdot2+1=3+2\sqrt2$. Their difference is $\sqrt2\ne0$, so the distinct pairs have distinct preactivations.

The feature set has two elements and both neighbor multisets have size one. Thus the example meets the countability and bound hypotheses of [F3], with irrational $\varepsilon$ established in step 1.1; the computed separation is a concrete instance of that injective coding condition.
